ui.office.talk.morning.1.a: Did you have breakfast this morning?
ui.office.talk.morning.1.b: Not yet, I was going to grab something downstairs.
ui.office.talk.morning.2.b: Yes, now I finally feel awake.
ui.office.talk.morning.3.a: Anything worth watching in the news today?
ui.office.talk.morning.3.b: I only skimmed it, I will read it properly later.
ui.office.talk.morning.4.a: Had a look at the prices this morning?
ui.office.talk.morning.4.b: Yes, I noted the few tickers to follow.
ui.office.talk.morning.5.a: What are you starting with today?
ui.office.talk.morning.6.a: Do you work better in the morning or the afternoon?
ui.office.talk.morning.6.b: Morning, my head is still clear.
ui.office.talk.noon.1.b: Not yet, I was thinking of the rice place nearby.
ui.office.talk.noon.2.b: Sure, give me a moment to put things away.
ui.office.talk.noon.3.a: The place nearby will be packed about now.
ui.office.talk.noon.3.b: Probably, we can still make it if we go early.
ui.office.talk.noon.5.b: A short nap and you are good as new.
ui.office.talk.noon.6.a: Packed lunch or eating out today?
ui.office.talk.noon.6.b: I brought lunch, easier to eat right here.
ui.office.talk.afternoon.1.b: Quite a bit, but I will make it.
ui.office.talk.afternoon.2.a: That coffee yesterday was really good.
ui.office.talk.afternoon.2.b: Let me buy you one tomorrow.
ui.office.talk.afternoon.4.a: This hour always makes me drowsy.
ui.office.talk.afternoon.4.b: Stand up and walk around, it helps.
ui.office.talk.afternoon.5.b: It really is, half the day is gone already.
ui.office.talk.afternoon.6.a: Shall we tidy our notes this afternoon?
ui.office.talk.afternoon.6.b: Yes, let us do it now and be done.
ui.office.talk.evening.1.b: Just a little longer, then I am heading home.
ui.office.talk.evening.2.b: Probably noodles at home, I am tired.
ui.office.talk.evening.3.b: Yes, but we got a lot done.
ui.office.talk.evening.4.b: By bus, a bit crowded at this hour.
ui.office.talk.evening.5.b: I wrote it down, ready for the morning.
ui.office.talk.evening.6.a: The street gets busy about now.
ui.office.talk.evening.6.b: Yes, everyone is on their way home.
ui.office.talk.night.1.b: Watching a bit longer, crypto never closes.
ui.office.talk.night.2.a: The office is so quiet now.
ui.office.talk.night.2.b: Yes, you can hear the air conditioner.
ui.office.talk.night.3.a: Tea? I am making some anyway.
ui.office.talk.night.3.b: Thanks, a hot cup for me.
ui.office.talk.night.4.b: One more look first, then I head out.
ui.office.talk.night.5.a: My eyes are tired from the screens.
ui.office.talk.night.5.b: Take a short break, I will keep watch.
ui.office.talk.night.6.a: Let us come in earlier tomorrow.
ui.office.talk.night.6.b: Okay, make sure you sleep enough.
ui.office.talk.rain.1.b: Probably going to last a while.
ui.office.talk.rain.2.b: Yes, but I will still get wet walking to the stop.
ui.office.talk.rain.3.a: We will be soaked going out for lunch.
ui.office.talk.rain.4.a: Rain and the traffic jams right away.
ui.office.talk.rain.4.b: Yes, getting home will take longer today.
ui.office.talk.rain.5.a: The sound of rain is soothing.
ui.office.talk.rain.5.b: Yes, easy to focus right now.
ui.office.talk.rain.6.a: Ginger tea for a rainy day?
ui.office.talk.rain.6.b: Good idea, one for me too.
ui.office.talk.rain.7.a: Look down the street, everyone is rushing.
ui.office.talk.rain.7.b: Yes, everyone has their raincoat on.
ui.office.talk.friday.1.b: Right on time, that is Friday afternoon for you.
ui.office.talk.friday.2.b: Yes, like a little reward for the week.
ui.office.talk.friday.3.b: Just that little cup over there.
ui.office.talk.friday.4.a: The week is over, what a relief.
ui.office.talk.friday.4.b: Yes, something sweet and then we carry on.
ui.office.talk.friday.5.a: I will grab one for each of us.
ui.office.talk.friday.5.b: Thanks, I will save our seats.
ui.office.talk.tet.1.a: The trees outside have Tet flowers now.
ui.office.talk.tet.1.b: Beautiful, it already feels like Tet.
ui.office.talk.tet.2.a: Going home for Tet this year?
ui.office.talk.tet.3.a: When does your Tet break start?
ui.office.talk.tet.4.a: The street Tet decorations are lovely.
ui.office.talk.tet.4.b: Yes, I look every time I walk past.
ui.office.talk.tet.5.a: I will clean the house before Tet, and you?
ui.office.talk.tet.5.b: I am on the candied fruit, just eating it is fun enough.
ui.office.talk.tet.6.a: Let us tidy our notes before the break.
ui.office.talk.trung-thu.1.a: Mid-Autumn is close, bought mooncakes yet?
ui.office.talk.trung-thu.1.b: Not yet, still choosing a flavour.
ui.office.talk.trung-thu.3.b: Yes, watching kids carry them is fun.
ui.office.talk.trung-thu.4.a: The streets are busier these days.
ui.office.talk.trung-thu.4.b: Yes, I avoid the main roads.
ui.office.talk.trung-thu.5.b: Yes, a slice for every desk.
ui.office.talk.trung-thu.6.a: The Mid-Autumn moon is always lovely.
ui.office.talk.trung-thu.6.b: Yes, look up on your way home.
ui.office.talk.quoc-khanh.1.a: National Day is near, going anywhere?
ui.office.talk.quoc-khanh.2.a: So many red flags on the street.
ui.office.talk.quoc-khanh.3.a: Did you check the holiday schedule?
ui.office.talk.quoc-khanh.3.b: Yes, let us wrap up before the break.
ui.office.talk.quoc-khanh.4.a: The roads will be busy on the holiday.
ui.office.talk.quoc-khanh.4.b: Yes, I plan to leave early.
ui.office.talk.quoc-khanh.5.a: Going back to your hometown for the holiday?
ui.office.talk.quoc-khanh.5.b: Yes, it has been a while.
ui.office.talk.quoc-khanh.6.a: Back to the routine after the holiday.
ui.office.talk.quoc-khanh.6.b: Yes, so enjoy the break while it lasts.
ui.office.talk.noel.1.a: The trees outside have Christmas lights now.
ui.office.talk.noel.2.b: Probably a get-together at a friend's, you?
ui.office.talk.noel.3.b: Not yet, still thinking about what to give.
ui.office.talk.noel.4.a: The streets are busy, everyone is shopping.
ui.office.talk.noel.4.b: Yes, even a quick errand takes squeezing through.
ui.office.talk.noel.5.a: The peppermint coffee is nice this season.
ui.office.talk.noel.5.b: Yes, I order it every time I pass the cafe.
ui.office.talk.noel.6.a: The year is almost over already.
ui.office.talk.noel.6.b: Yes, I am starting the year review.
ui.office.talk.preopen.1.b: Yes, I already went through the last session's closing prices.
ui.office.talk.preopen.2.a: Which ticker do you look at first today?
ui.office.talk.preopen.3.a: The office is already buzzing before the open.
ui.office.talk.preopen.3.b: Yes, everyone wants to know the picture early.
ui.office.talk.preopen.4.a: Anything notable in this morning's news?
ui.office.talk.preopen.4.b: A couple of items, I am saving them for the morning meeting.
ui.office.talk.preopen.5.a: How do you think today's session will go?
ui.office.talk.preopen.5.b: No idea, let us watch the first few minutes.
ui.office.talk.preopen.6.b: Good idea, there is just enough time.
ui.office.talk.open.1.a: Trading is on, which tickers are you watching?
ui.office.talk.open.2.a: How does the market feel today?
ui.office.talk.open.2.b: Lively, but I am still waiting.
ui.office.talk.open.3.a: No rush, wait for a clearer signal.
ui.office.talk.open.4.a: Which tickers is everyone piling into?
ui.office.talk.open.5.a: Step out now and you might miss the move.
ui.office.talk.open.5.b: I will wait out this stretch, then make coffee.
ui.office.talk.open.6.a: Did you write down your reason for buying?
ui.office.talk.open.6.b: Yes, always, so I can look back later.
ui.office.talk.lunch.1.a: The market is on its lunch break, let us eat.
ui.office.talk.lunch.1.b: Yes, then we will be sharp when it reopens.
ui.office.talk.lunch.2.a: Lunch break, no more price checking?
ui.office.talk.lunch.2.b: No, I will look when it reopens this afternoon.
ui.office.talk.lunch.3.a: The afternoon session might differ from the morning.
ui.office.talk.lunch.4.a: The screens are still bright at lunch.
ui.office.talk.lunch.4.b: Yes, I will turn some off to rest my eyes.
ui.office.talk.lunch.5.a: What are you eating on the break?
ui.office.talk.lunch.5.b: A lunch box, quick, so I can nap.
ui.office.talk.lunch.6.a: Did any ticker surprise you this morning?
ui.office.talk.lunch.6.b: One of them, I will see how it goes this afternoon.
ui.office.talk.closed.1.a: The market has closed, what a relief.
ui.office.talk.closed.1.b: Yes, now I will go back over the session.
ui.office.talk.closed.2.a: How did the session feel to you?
ui.office.talk.closed.2.b: Tense at times, fine in the end.
ui.office.talk.closed.3.b: Working on them, with the reason for each ticker.
ui.office.talk.closed.4.a: Any ticker to watch more closely next session?
ui.office.talk.closed.4.b: Yes, I have already marked them.
ui.office.talk.closed.5.b: Yes, a hot one for me.
ui.office.talk.closed.6.a: The end of the session is often jumpy.
ui.office.talk.closed.6.b: Yes, so I do not rush to conclusions.
ui.office.talk.weekend.1.a: The market is closed today, so quiet.
ui.office.talk.weekend.2.b: Yes, going over my notes from the last session.
ui.office.talk.weekend.3.a: Anything to prepare for the next session?
ui.office.talk.weekend.3.b: Writing down the tickers to follow is enough.
ui.office.talk.weekend.4.a: Going anywhere on your day off?
ui.office.talk.weekend.4.b: Probably resting at home with a book.
ui.office.talk.weekend.5.a: The office is so empty today.
ui.office.talk.weekend.5.b: Yes, a nice chance to work in peace.
ui.office.talk.weekend.6.a: Crypto keeps going even on a day off.
ui.office.talk.weekend.6.b: Yes, so I still keep an eye on it.
ui.office.talk.down.1.a: The market's in the red today, isn't it?
ui.office.talk.down.1.b: Yes, the selling pressure must still be heavy.
ui.office.talk.down.2.a: The index is down today, are you worried?
ui.office.talk.down.2.b: A little, but I will review the plan first.
ui.office.talk.down.3.a: The whole board is sliding, discouraging.
ui.office.talk.down.3.b: Stay calm, let us see which tickers hold up.
ui.office.talk.down.4.a: The index is down today, let us not decide in a hurry.
ui.office.talk.down.4.b: Right, wait until it is clearer.
ui.office.talk.down.5.a: With the market down, buy more or wait?
ui.office.talk.down.6.a: Are the big names dragging the index down?

slash.tradingProfileUsage:
Usage
/profile (or /profile show)
/profile set <field> <value>
/profile enable|disable <segment>
/profile reset

Examples
/profile set risk-level balanced
/profile set reserve-pct-nav 20%
/profile set segment-target crypto 0.1

Shares: write 20% or 0.2.
Segments: {segments}

Risk appetite
risk-level: one setting for all of it -
conservative, balanced or aggressive. It also
sets the limits below.
risk-capacity: how much loss you can afford.
risk-willingness: how much loss you are
comfortable with.
These two take the same three levels, but not
in the same write as risk-level.

Horizon and goal
horizon <segment> <short|long>: hold each segment
for the short or the long term.
goal <{goals}>: preserve capital,
steady income or growth.

Buying limits (share of your total assets)
reserve-pct-nav: cash you always keep.
risk-per-trade-pct-nav: most you may lose if one
new buy hits its stop-loss.
maximum-open-risk-pct-nav: most you may lose if
every holding hits its stop-loss together.
maximum-sector-pct-nav: most you may put in one
sector.
regime-scale: most of the amount you plan to buy
that is used each time (0.75 uses 75%). A
defensive market can lower it further.

Buying and selling in steps
entry-tranche-pct is how much of a new buy goes in
first (0.5 = half now, half once the plan holds).
take-profit-tranche-pct is how much you sell at the
first target; the rest keeps running with a
stop-loss that only moves up.
Both take 0.2 to 1.

Target or cap - which one you want
segment-target <segment> <fraction>: the share of
your book a segment is steered towards. Set it
and the other segments give up their share of
the difference, so the targets still total 100%.
This is the one that moves money. Your cash
reserve is never touched, and a target that would
eat into it is refused.
A target you set is kept: changing risk-level or
turning a segment on or off recalculates everything
around it rather than over it. reset clears it,
and so does turning that segment off.

segment-cap <segment> <fraction>: the most of your
book a segment may reach.
position-cap <segment> <fraction>: the most any one
stock or coin in the segment may take.
A cap is only room: raising one lets a buy fill
further, it moves nothing there.
Lowering segment-cap pulls the limits under it down
with it, and is refused below the segment's target.
A segment you turned off takes neither.

What turning a segment off does
Its limits close: nothing in that segment is sized
or bought.
The remaining segments' targets are recalculated as
if it had never existed; turning it back on
recalculates them again with it.
risk-level recalculates every limit but keeps the
segments you turned off.
reset goes back to the default segments and keeps
your watchlist.

trading.brief.story.hook.breadth-split-index-dow: The VN-Index closed red, yet more stocks rose than fell. So who is dragging it down?
trading.brief.story.insight.breadth-split-index-: The pressure sits in a small group of large caps. Most of the market is in better shape than the index makes it look.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.breadth-split-i: One lopsided session is not a trend. It needs a few more sessions, with money coming in behind it.
trading.brief.story.hook.breadth-split-index-up: The VN-Index is green, yet most stocks are red. Who is this rally leaning on?
trading.brief.story.insight.breadth-split-index-: A few large caps are carrying the index while most stocks sit it out. Rallies like this tend to be fragile.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.breadth-split-i: If money spreads to other names, this could just be the opening of a broader rally.
trading.brief.story.hook.foreign-selling: Foreign investors have sold heavily over the last {sessions} sessions. The question is how long the market can absorb it.
trading.brief.story.insight.foreign-selling: When foreign selling is steady, the large caps they hold most are usually the first to feel it.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.foreign-selling: Proprietary desks and local investors may step in, and foreign flows can turn around quickly.
trading.brief.story.hook.foreign-buying: Foreign investors keep buying steadily. What do they see that the market does not?
trading.brief.story.insight.foreign-buying: Steady foreign buying is usually solid support for the large caps.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.foreign-buying: It may just be funds rebalancing, rather than a bet on the whole market.
trading.brief.story.hook.turnover-thin-rise: The index rose sharply, but little money came in. Are enough people behind this rise yet?
trading.brief.story.insight.turnover-thin-rise: A rise on thin turnover turns around easily once people start taking profit.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.turnover-thin-r: Low turnover can simply mean sellers have run out, which makes prices easier to lift.
trading.brief.story.hook.turnover-thin-fall: The index fell sharply, but few people were selling. Is anyone really panicking?
trading.brief.story.insight.turnover-thin-fall: A fall with few people taking part is usually not a rout yet.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.turnover-thin-f: It may also mean buyers are staying away, so prices can keep sliding until they return.
trading.brief.story.hook.turnover-heavy-rise: The index rose sharply on turnover well above normal. Has big money come back?
trading.brief.story.insight.turnover-heavy-rise: A rise with turnover behind it deserves more trust than a lone bounce.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.turnover-heavy-: A turnover spike sometimes marks a short-term top, as holders use the strength to get out.
trading.brief.story.hook.turnover-heavy-fall: The index fell sharply and turnover jumped. Is this a rout, or are the sellers nearly done?
trading.brief.story.insight.turnover-heavy-fall: A fall on heavy turnover means the selling pressure is real, not noise.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.turnover-heavy-: Heavy sell-offs sometimes clear out everyone who wanted to leave, and open the way for a rebound.
trading.brief.story.hook.support-test: The VN-Index is sitting right on its support zone of recent months. Will it hold?
trading.brief.story.insight.support-test: Support is where buyers stepped in before. If it holds, the risk of a deeper fall gets smaller.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.support-test: A break below support usually brings another wave of selling, since many stop-losses sit just under it.
trading.brief.story.hook.resistance-test: The VN-Index has climbed right up to resistance. Will sellers show up here again?
trading.brief.story.insight.resistance-test: Resistance is where people who bought higher earlier tend to sell to get their money back.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.resistance-test: If the index clears resistance on good turnover, the old ceiling can become the new floor.
trading.brief.story.hook.breadth-widening: In just {sessions} sessions, the number of stocks above their 50-day average jumped. Is the market really getting healthier?
trading.brief.story.insight.breadth-widening: When many stocks improve together, a rise stands on a wider base and usually lasts longer.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.breadth-widenin: A quick improvement from a low level may only be a technical bounce after heavy selling.
trading.brief.story.hook.breadth-narrowing: In just {sessions} sessions, the number of stocks above their 50-day average fell sharply. Is the market weakening underneath?
trading.brief.story.insight.breadth-narrowing: When fewer and fewer stocks hold their trend, the index runs out of breath easily.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.breadth-narrowi: Sometimes the market is just catching its breath before money picks a new sector.
trading.brief.story.hook.sector-leading: The {sector} sector is clearly stronger than the market. Has money picked it?
trading.brief.story.insight.sector-leading: When a sector leads for a while, the rest of its names usually get pulled along.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.sector-leading: A sector that breaks out while most of the market is weak is also quick to see profit-taking.
trading.brief.story.hook.sector-lagging: The {sector} sector is clearly weaker than the market. Does someone already know something?
trading.brief.story.insight.sector-lagging: A sector that lags for long usually reflects the business, not just the price.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.sector-lagging: An oversold sector is sometimes where the sharpest rebound comes once sentiment turns.
trading.brief.story.hook.basis-premium: The VN30 future trades well above the index itself. Are derivatives traders betting on a rise?
trading.brief.story.insight.basis-premium: A wide positive gap shows derivatives buyers are willing to pay up for a position.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.basis-premium: The gap tends to close by itself near expiry, not necessarily because the market turned.
trading.brief.story.hook.basis-discount: The VN30 future trades well below the index itself. Are derivatives traders turning defensive?
trading.brief.story.insight.basis-discount: A wide negative gap often means derivatives sellers are moving ahead of the stock market.
trading.brief.story.counterpoint.basis-discount: Funds selling futures to hedge can push the price down without forecasting a fall.

social.fetchFailed: Couldn't reach {url}. Check the address and try again.
social.fetchTooLarge: {url} is bigger than {bytes} bytes, which is far more than any skill needs, so it wasn't installed.
social.noApiBase: This skill doesn't say where its API lives. Add `--api-base <https URL>` if you know it.
social.notRest: This network speaks GraphQL or RPC, and only REST networks can be joined.
social.otherApiHost: The skill sends API calls to more than one host, so it can't be pinned safely.
social.authScheme: The skill asks for a login other than a bearer key, which isn't supported.
social.fileElsewhere: The skill lists {url}, which isn't on the skill's own site, so it can't be pinned.
social.fileNameClash: Two files in the skill share the name {name}.
social.badName: "{name}" can't be a network name: use lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 32.
social.badApiBase: {url} can't be an API address: it must be a public https host on the normal port, with no login in it.
social.pinDamaged: The pinned files for this network are damaged. Run `{brand} social rollback {network}` or add it again.
social.fileNotPinned: {file} isn't one of the files pinned for {network}.
social.nameTaken: There's already a network called {network}. Pick another with `--name`.
social.unknownNetwork: There's no network called {network}. `{brand} social list` shows what you have.
social.labelUnknown: {endpoint} isn't an endpoint in this skill.
social.pendingChanged: {network} changed its skill again while you were reading. Run `{brand} social update {network}` to see the newer one.
social.noPrevious: {network} has no earlier version to go back to.
social.networkHasMembers: {agents} still on {network}. Take each off first with `{brand} social leave <agent> {network}`, or just pause the network with `{brand} social pause {network}`.
social.agentNotUser: {agent} is a built-in agent. Only agents you made can join a network.
social.agentPaused: {agent} is paused. Resume it first with `{brand} agent resume {agent}`.
social.needsFocus: {agent} shares your own focus, so its calls are your book's plan. Give it its own `[focus]` before it talks in public.
social.toolsOutside: {agent} holds tools a networked agent may not have: {tools}. Take them out of its `agent.toml`.
social.networkPaused: {network} is paused. `{brand} social resume {network}` turns it back on.
social.needsKeyEnv: {network}'s skill doesn't show how to register, so pass the key you got from them: `{brand} social join <agent> {network} --key-env <VAR>`.
social.nameTakenOnNetwork: {network} already has someone called {name}. Choose another public name with `--name`.
social.registerUnreachable: Couldn't reach {network} to register. Check your connection and try again in a few minutes.
social.registerNoKey: {network} registered the agent but sent back no key. Nothing was saved.
social.keySaveFailed: {network} registered the agent, but its key couldn't be saved here. Use this to reset the key from {network}'s side: {claims}
social.refusedNeedsRekey: {network} turned {agent}'s key away. Get a new key from them, then `{brand} social rekey {agent} {network} --key-env <VAR>`.
social.noticeSkillChanged: {network} changed its skill ({files} files, {endpoints} endpoints differ). Nothing changes for your agents until you look: `{brand} social update {network}`.
social.noticePinMismatch: The pinned files for {network} changed on disk, so I paused it. If you didn't edit them, roll back: `{brand} social rollback {network}`.
social.noticeKeyRefused: {network} turned {agent}'s key away, so it's off that network until you rekey: `{brand} social rekey {agent} {network} --key-env <VAR>`.
social.noticeMemberPaused: {network} refused {agent} five times in a row, so I paused it there. Check the agent's claim, then `{brand} social resume {network} {agent}`.
social.noticeDraftWaiting: {agent} wants to send something on {network} that needs your OK ({reason}). See it with `/social drafts`, or `{brand} social drafts` on the computer.
social.draftReasonReview: every post from this agent is reviewed first
social.draftCut: (cut here; the full text is longer)
social.draftOlderSkill: Made before {network} changed its skill; it's checked against the new one when you approve.
social.approveFailed: Draft {id} didn't go through; it's still waiting. Here is what the network said:
social.approveMaybeLive: Draft {id} may already be live: the network never confirmed it. Check the network before approving it again; it's still waiting. Here is what came back:
social.needsVerification: The network is holding this until a quick check is answered, and only a running agent can answer it in time. It may stay hidden and count as one failed check. Don't send it again by hand; if it matters, let the agent write it fresh on its next visit.
social.noDrafts: 📝 No drafts are waiting for your review.
social.noSuchDraft: There's no waiting draft {id}. `/social drafts` or `{brand} social drafts` lists them.
social.tooManyEndpoints: The skill lists more than {max} endpoints, far more than a network needs, so it wasn't installed.
social.tooManyFiles: The skill lists more than {max} files, which is far more than a skill needs, so it wasn't installed.
